marta: Heads-up — found a regression in an end-to-end perfetto trace (client->gateway->runtime). link: https://perfetto.dev/trace/ABCDEF123
marta: Symptoms: ~12-18ms tail inside the runtime span on bursty short requests. Kernel selection is oscillating between quantized int8 and fp16 kernels, and KV cache miss rate spikes to ~30% at request step 2.
dan: Which model/config? reproducible for you?
marta: gpt-small-qlora, seq_len=1024, dynamic batching enabled at gateway. Happens when 6-12 short paralell requests hit within the batching window.
ryan: Can you paste the perfetto filter you used and any nsys snippets?
marta: Perfetto query I used:
```
slice.name:kernel_selector::choose_kernel OR annotation:"kv_cache_miss"
trace.process_name:runtime
```
And a quick nsys command we ran:
```
nsys profile --output=run.nsys --trace=nvtx,cuda python -m repro.load_test
```
I uploaded nvprof/nsys zips to the thread.
perf-bot: Automated trace summary: extra tail 11.9ms median, hotspots: kernel_selector::choose_kernel (44%), KVCache::lookup (26%), small_matmul_kernel (18%).
kai: Could be hysteresis missing in kernel selector. If batch size oscillates between 1-3, selector flips and incurs kernel launch penalties.
dan: I can repro locally. Running with --batching=off reduces tail to ~3ms, which points at batching interaction.
marta: Additional observation: many of the small kernels have <512 threads and show high launch overhead in nvprof. Also we log "kernel_choice: fallback" intermittently right before KV cache miss spikes.
ryan: Hypothesis: gateway batching boundary alignment causes prefix KV lookups to mismatch (alignment -> miss), which triggers extra work and leads to smaller effective batches in runtime, causing kernel selection thrash.
kai: Quick experiments to try:
- force kernel policy to fp16 (bypass selector) and measure
- add 50ms hysteresis in kernel selector when batch_size < 4
- add perfetto annotations for gateway batching windows
marta: Action items:
1) add perfetto events at gateway for each batching window + request group id (so we can correlate client boundary -> runtime traces)
2) add telemetry counter for kernel-selection events and transitions
3) implement selector hysteresis and test on canary
4) instrument KV cache to report prefix alignment metrics
dan: I'll open a small PR: "selector: add hysteresis for tiny batches". Plan: default 50ms, opt-out via runtime flag. Will run perfetto/ nsight afterwards.
perf-bot: Perf test run recorded: run_id=run-20260310-17, baseline median tail 11.5ms, post-hysteresis try 9.2ms (-20%). Data and traces attached.
kai: If that holds, also add a unit/regression test: synthetic load of 10k short requests asserting KV miss rate <5% and median tail <6ms.
marta: Uploaded repro script: repro/short_burst_runner.py and nsys/nvprof outputs in artifacts/1770456789.zip. Please comment on PR when you run.
dan: ack. starting local test now. Will post perfetto link when done.
ryan: Nice find — tagging eng-sre to watch for any canary alerts: @eng-sre
marta: Thanks all. If anyone spots other traces with similar pattern, drop links here.
:thumbsup:
